title: Peptide peddlers cheer as RFK Jr. unilaterally grants access, overruling FDA
gist: HHS Secretary Robert F. Kennedy issued an enforcement-discretion policy letting 503A compounding pharmacies make six peptides (BPC-157, Epitalon, KPV, MOTS-c, Semax, TB-500) that FDA removed in 2023 over safety concerns. The rationale leans on an advisory vote from a committee Kennedy stacked with peptide-linked members; sellers celebrated while CSPI and ASEM warned of harms and weakened trial incentives.

insights.claim: Kennedy's rule does not change the peptides' regulatory status; HHS will simply stop taking enforcement action against compounding pharmacies making them, effectively greenlighting production and sales.
insights.speaker: Beth Mole
insights.so_what: Non-enforcement policies can open markets quickly but are reversible by a future administration.
insights.quote: The rule does not change the regulatory status of the peptide; instead, it states the Department of Health and Human Services (HHS) will no longer take enforcement action
